fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`.provision.log` is written into a worktree when its venv is provisioned, but it is not
listed in `.gitignore`. Because it is untracked-and-not-ignored, `git status --porcelain`
is non-empty for the life of the worktree.

That is not merely cosmetic. The machine-local worktree GC
(`com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc`) refuses to reclaim any worktree whose status is
non-empty — the "no uncommitted work" safety guard. A provisioning artifact therefore
pins a worktree permanently: it can never age out, and no amount of idleness makes it
collectable. A 2026-08-06 audit of this checkout found 6 worktrees whose ONLY untracked
file was `.provision.log`, plus the same guard firing on in-scope agent worktrees
(`KEEP agent-a1bf191c510431899: dirty`).

The file is pure build/provisioning noise: it records the output of venv creation and the
editable install. Nothing reads it after provisioning, and it is never intended to be
committed.

## Approach

Add `.provision.log` to `.gitignore`, next to the other provisioning/rebuild noise
entries (`.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`) so it sits with the
artifacts it belongs to rather than at the end of the file.

An unanchored `.provision.log` pattern is deliberate: the file is written at whatever
directory the provisioner runs in, so matching it at any depth is the intended behavior,
consistent with how `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` are already written in this file.

This is a one-line mechanical change to a config file. It does not alter any Python
source, any CLI behavior, or any gate.

## Scope

- `.gitignore` — add one entry.

No other file changes. No `src/rebar` change, so no test-file change is implied.

## Testing

No new testable behavior is added: `.gitignore` is consumed by git itself, not by any
rebar code path, and no test imports or executes it. Verification is therefore direct
observation of git's own behavior plus the repo's existing gates:

- `git check-ignore -v .provision.log` exits 0 and names the new `.gitignore` line
  (before the change it exits 1).
- With a `.provision.log` present in a clean worktree, `git status --porcelain` is empty
  (before the change it reports `?? .provision.log`).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass (enforced by the pre-commit hook).
- CI's `Verified` label on the Gerrit change is `+1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `.gitignore` contains a `.provision.log` entry; checked by
      `grep -c '^\.provision\.log$' .gitignore` returning 1.
- [x] `git check-ignore -v .provision.log` exits 0 and attributes the match to
      `.gitignore`.
- [x] In a clean checkout with a `.provision.log` file created, `git status --porcelain`
      produces no output.
- [x] No file other than `.gitignore` is modified by the change; checked by
      `git show --name-only` listing exactly that one path.
- [x] The change reaches `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on Gerrit and is submitted to
      `main`.
